title: The First Form - Anthropos and Adam Kadmon
author: Ethan James Farrell
description: A custom cosmological study from Ethan's collection (2026): The First Form: Anthropos, Adam Kadmon, and the Cosmology of the Primordial Human. It asks why the universe was imagined in the shape of a human being, reading Gnostic and Jewish mystical cosmologies against scripture and later interpretation. Opening with Ezekiel's vision of the likeness of a man upon the sapphire throne, its chapters move through scriptural seeds in Genesis and the prophets, Philo's heavenly human of Alexandria, the form on the Merkavah chariot, the Anthropos in Gnostic cosmologies, Adam Elyon and the emergence of Adam Kadmon, and Isaac Luria's doctrine of contraction (tzimtzum), the line of light and the primordial man. Closing chapters set out the shared grammar and divergent worlds of the two traditions, reasonable expansions, common and individual beliefs, and 'the face that precedes the world'. It is a companion to the library's other Anthropos volumes.
